scheme_name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture Sub Scheme Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan Region- Meghalaya
description:
The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing horticultural production and improving the livelihoods of farmers. 

This scheme was launched in 2014 as part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture under the National Mission for Agricultural Extension and Technology. 

The Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan Region specifically targets the unique challenges and opportunities in these regions. 

Meghalaya is one of the states that benefit from this mission. 

The primary objective of this sub-scheme is to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector in the North Eastern states, including Meghalaya. 

The initiative aims to increase the area under horticulture crops from 1.5 million hectares to 2 million hectares by 2025. 

It also seeks to enhance the productivity of horticulture crops by 30 percent during the same period. 

The scheme focuses on various horticultural crops such as fruits, vegetables, spices, and flowers. 

Specific targets include increasing the production of fruits like oranges, pineapples, and bananas, which are significant in Meghalaya. 

The benefits under this scheme include financial assistance for the establishment of nurseries, production of quality planting materials, and the development of post-harvest infrastructure. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh for setting up a nursery. 

Financial assistance is also provided for the construction of packhouses and cold storage facilities, with grants covering up to 50 percent of the total cost. 

The scheme also offers training programs for farmers to enhance their skills in modern horticulture practices. 

Eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a resident of Meghalaya and being engaged in horticulture farming. 

Farmers must also have a minimum landholding of 0.5 hectares to qualify for assistance. 

The age limit for applicants is set at 18 years and above. 

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed INR 2 lakh to qualify for financial assistance. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must first visit the local horticulture department office to obtain the application form. 

They must fill out the form with accurate details and submit it along with required documents. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card, land ownership documents, and a bank account statement. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local horticulture officer. 

The officer will conduct a field visit to verify the details provided in the application. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The timeline for application submission typically runs from April to June every year. 

Disbursement of funds usually occurs within two months of approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme in Meghalaya is the Department of Horticulture, Government of Meghalaya. 

Farmers can contact the department at their headquarters in Shillong for more information. 

The contact number for the Department of Horticulture is +91-364-250-0000. 

Additionally, the department has a website where farmers can find more information about the scheme and other horticulture-related initiatives. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in horticulture. 

It encourages the use of organic farming methods and integrated pest management. 

The government aims to promote the use of bio-fertilizers and bio-pesticides to reduce chemical inputs. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the marketing of horticulture produce through the establishment of farmer producer organizations. 

These organizations will help farmers in collective marketing and better price realization for their produce. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 2,000 crore for the entire Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture for the period from 2021 to 2025. 

Out of this, a significant portion is earmarked for the North East and Himalayan regions. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in the horticulture sector. 

It is expected to generate around 10 lakh jobs in the horticulture value chain by 2025. 

The government is also focusing on improving the quality of horticulture produce through better research and development. 

Collaboration with agricultural universities and research institutions is a key component of this initiative. 

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and aims to empower women farmers by providing them with equal access to resources and training. 

Special provisions are made for women self-help groups to participate in horticulture activities. 

The government also plans to organize horticulture fairs and exhibitions to promote the produce of Meghalaya. 

These events will provide a platform for farmers to showcase their products and connect with potential buyers. 

The impact of this scheme is expected to be significant in improving the livelihoods of farmers in Meghalaya. 

The focus on horticulture is particularly relevant given the state's favorable climate for growing a variety of fruits and vegetables. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of this scheme reach the intended beneficiaries effectively. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted to assess its impact and make necessary adjustments. 

The Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture represents a comprehensive approach to enhancing the horticulture sector in Meghalaya. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable horticulture ecosystem that benefits farmers and contributes to the state's economy. 

The initiative is part of the broader vision of the Government of India to promote agricultural development and improve food security. 

Through this scheme, the government is taking significant steps towards achieving these goals in the North Eastern region. 

Overall, the Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan Region is a vital program that holds the potential to transform the horticulture landscape in Meghalaya. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of the opportunities provided by this scheme to improve their agricultural practices and enhance their income. 

The government remains committed to supporting farmers in their horticultural endeavors through various initiatives and programs. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's focus on sustainable agricultural development and rural empowerment.
